sections.heading: Build a small, verifiable product shortlist
paragraphs: Open the original seller page for each candidate and record the product, colour, size, quantity and included pieces. Clothing needs a usable measurement chart; footwear needs the chart for the exact model. A seller photo or catalogue title cannot establish stock, authenticity or fit. If a listing combines several options, confirm that the displayed price belongs to your chosen one. Keep the original source URL so that you can identify the order if the listing changes later.

For a first purchase, a small shortlist with clear specifications is easier to manage than a large collection of uncertain links. Resolve questions about size and construction before payment. If the automatic form cannot read a seller link, follow the official manual purchase process and confirm the details with the purchaser. Do not substitute a different listing simply because its photograph looks similar. The seller, return conditions and measurement chart may all be different.

sections.heading: Keep the purchasing and shipping budgets separate
paragraphs: Record the item cost and domestic delivery to the warehouse first. Then estimate international delivery using Poland as the destination and a realistic description of the goods. Include packing, optional services and any charges shown in the current quote. If you compare values in different currencies, record the actual conversion and payment conditions offered at checkout. An old exchange-rate screenshot or another buyer’s total is not a reliable budget for your own order.

Do not add unsupported claims such as free returns, no payment fees or guaranteed tax-free delivery to your plan. Read what each displayed amount covers and which charges remain separate. Route names can describe a service without settling every possible destination obligation. Use accurate contents and values when completing required shipment information. If the quote or instructions are unclear, ask the provider to explain the specific charge before confirming the parcel rather than guessing a declaration value.

sections.heading: Prepare the Polish delivery details carefully
paragraphs: Use the recipient’s actual name, complete street address, building and apartment details where applicable, postal code, city and a reachable contact method. Check each field in the official order form rather than pasting the whole address into an arbitrary box. Keep any delivery instructions concise. Do not assume that an international line supports a parcel locker or collection point unless that option is explicitly available in the selected service.

Before payment, read the address back as the carrier will receive it. A missing apartment identifier can matter even when the city and postal code are correct. If you need to change an address after submission, use the official support process promptly and ask whether the shipment is still editable. Avoid publishing personal address or tracking details on public forums. Share the information required to resolve a delivery problem through the account or the carrier’s official channel.

sections.heading: Review the warehouse before choosing a parcel
paragraphs: A domestic tracking event marked delivered normally refers to delivery to the warehouse at that stage of the purchase. It is not evidence that an international parcel has reached Poland. Wait for the corresponding order information and review the available inspection photos, size and quantity. Ask for a specific additional measurement or image when it would resolve a real uncertainty. Check any cost before requesting an optional service.

Record the storage date and return decision for each item separately. Normal storage time and the seller’s return window are different. If an item is wrong or visibly damaged, raise the issue while the relevant return process is still available; do not wait merely because another seller has not dispatched. Keep labels, packaging and included accessories intact while a return is being considered. Combine only the goods you have decided to keep, subject to the available shipping restrictions.

sections.heading: Compare the routes returned for your actual parcel
paragraphs: Use the same destination, contents, packed weight and dimensions for each route comparison. Note the quoted total, estimated transit window, size and weight restrictions, and available delivery or cover conditions. Read how the route calculates chargeable weight. A large light parcel may be billed on volume for an applicable line, so dividing the shipping total by the number of items can hide the real cost driver.

Treat the displayed transit estimate as an estimate for its stated stage. Seller preparation, domestic delivery, inspection and packing happen before or around the international leg and may not be included. For an event or gift with a fixed date, allow for the complete sequence and the uncertainty of carrier handling. This guide cannot name a universally fastest or cheapest line because available services and their conditions can change with the contents and current quotation.

sections.heading: Track the international shipment to Poland
paragraphs: After dispatch, open the parcel record in the official account and use the tracking information attached to that shipment. Keep the purchase order number, domestic seller tracking and international parcel number separate. A label-created event shows that a record exists; a collection scan provides different evidence. Read the date and wording of the latest event before concluding that the parcel is moving, waiting for information or ready for local delivery.

If tracking stops changing, send a concise support request with the parcel number, selected route, latest event and its date. Ask which stage is pending and whether you need to provide anything. Do not open repeated cases that omit the existing reference. If the carrier requests information, verify the official channel and respond accurately. Once local delivery information is available, follow the carrier’s instructions rather than assuming that an earlier estimate overrides a later delivery notice.

As a planning example, imagine that a jacket is already stored while a shirt is still with its seller. Check the jacket’s return decision and storage deadline before deciding to wait. Compare the cost and timing of a combined parcel only when the available information supports that comparison. The newest item should not determine every deadline in the order, and a possible shipping saving should be weighed against the delay and the conditions attached to each item.

sections.heading: Receive the parcel and keep useful evidence
paragraphs: Inspect the outer packaging and label on receipt, and keep them while checking the contents. Record an obvious shortage or damage clearly and contact the relevant carrier or Kakobuy promptly under the current reporting requirements. A photograph should show the real issue and enough context to identify the parcel or item. Keep private account and payment details out of public posts when asking for general advice.

Finish your purchase record with the actual delivered cost, final parcel measurements and any measurements of clothing you decide to keep. These details make a later order easier to plan, but they still do not guarantee that the same route or seller terms will remain available. Use the related shipping calculator, tracking and refund guides below for the next specific question. The best next action is the one supported by the current order record, not by an unrelated buyer’s timeline.

Similar front photographs do not establish that the cut, fabric, patches or contents of the package are identical.

sections.heading: Understand version labels without assuming their meaning
paragraphs: Terms such as player version, fan version and retro are used by sellers to distinguish products, but the label alone does not define a consistent size chart or material standard. Ask what is different in that specific listing. Compare the stated cut, collar, sleeve construction, fabric description and decoration method. Treat claims about official licensing or authenticity separately from the style description. If an officially licensed shirt is essential to your purchase, choose a source that can provide appropriate evidence. This guide explains selection and inspection questions; it does not certify sellers, recommend counterfeit versions or turn a catalogue name into proof of origin.

sections.heading: Use the correct size chart and a comparable shirt
paragraphs: Lay a football shirt that already fits flat and measure it consistently. Record the chest width, body length and relevant sleeve measurement, noting the exact start and end points. Compare with a reference intended for the same use. A tight training layer is not a useful reference for a loose shirt worn over other clothing unless you deliberately want that difference. Keep the seller’s stated units and tolerance alongside your measurements.

Confirm whether the chart gives garment dimensions or recommended body measurements. A flat chest width is not the same as a full circumference, and a general height-and-weight suggestion cannot describe every body shape. Check whether each version or age range has its own chart. If a number appears implausible or the measurement method is missing, request clarification before selecting the size. sections.heading: Confirm names, numbers and patches before customisation
paragraphs: If you choose personalisation, provide the spelling, capitalisation, number and placement exactly as required by the seller’s order process. Check whether the printing option applies to the selected shirt version and whether a patch shown in the image is included or optional. Save the written selection and any confirmation. Read the return conditions before authorising custom work. Do not assume that you can decide on a printed name later or reverse a completed customisation because another size looks preferable. Resolve size and design questions first, then confirm the final instructions through the official order record.

sections.heading: Compare the total offer and the original source
paragraphs: When comparing candidates, include the chosen variant, printing or patch options, domestic delivery and any minimum quantity. The lowest displayed price may describe an unprinted shirt or a different size range. Record the original seller URL rather than only a catalogue identifier. If the listing is no longer available, a similar image from another source is a new purchase decision with its own chart, options and terms.

Keep international shipping separate from the product comparison until you have an appropriate parcel estimate. A shirt-only order and a kit with extra pieces have different contents, and combining several orders changes the packed weight. Do not claim an exact delivered price from the catalogue thumbnail. Use the official estimator with the destination and plausible parcel inputs, then replace assumptions with measured information when the goods reach the warehouse.

sections.heading: Prepare an inspection checklist for your own order
paragraphs: After warehouse arrival, compare the order-specific images with the selected design, colour, size, quantity and included pieces. Inspect the front and back, collar, sleeve details and visible decoration. For personalised items, compare the lettering and number with the written confirmation. Do not interpret a clean-looking badge as authentication or a flat photograph as proof of comfortable fit. If you need a measurement, specify the method and compare it with the same method used on your reference garment. Report a clear discrepancy promptly and keep the evidence tied to the correct order rather than combining photos from several similar shirts.

sections.heading: Resolve problems before packing the international parcel
paragraphs: If the shirt is the wrong variant, visibly damaged or inconsistent with an agreed customisation, state the issue precisely and ask about the available remedy. Keep labels, packaging and accessories while the case is open. A request, seller approval, physical return and refund are separate steps. Do not assume that a storage allowance extends a return window or that an international shipment can be recalled easily once the parcel has been submitted.

For shirts you keep, ask for packaging appropriate to the fabric and decoration. Avoid promising that every print or badge tolerates the same compression. Read any supplied care instructions rather than inventing a universal wash temperature. When combining items, check the current route restrictions and final packed measurements. Optional services should solve a stated need; adding them automatically can increase cost without answering the fit or condition question that mattered in the first place.

For a concrete comparison, consider an unprinted loose shirt and a fitted personalised version offered on the same page. Record the chart and selected price for each separately. Confirm whether the printed version can still be returned if its agreed specifications are met but you dislike the fit. This question belongs before customisation. Treating the page as a single interchangeable product can hide both the measurement difference and the change in return conditions.

The table below provides a starting point. This is more useful than a list of popular team names because it records the facts needed to repeat or improve a decision. If a seller changes the listing, your saved variant information also makes a support request easier to understand.

After delivery, check the received item against the order and record the measurements that worked for you. Keep the parcel evidence until any delivery concern is resolved. For the next purchase, revisit the current chart even if the shirt looks similar: a different seller or version may use different proportions. Follow the related sizing, QC and return guides below when you need a more detailed check, and use the official account for decisions about your actual order.

sections.heading: Start with the decision you need to make
paragraphs: A useful Kakobuy spreadsheet helps you move from a broad idea to a specific seller listing. It should make the product, selected variant and next verification step easier to understand. A large item count or a confident recommendation cannot tell you whether a jacket fits, whether a seller still has stock or what delivery to your country will cost. Begin with your purpose: finding a category, comparing a few candidates or checking a product you have already chosen.

The word spreadsheet is used for both shared tables and searchable catalogue websites. Either format can be helpful when its links are usable and its limits are clear. Kakobuy Pick is an independent catalogue and reading resource; orders, payments, warehouse inspection and international shipping take place in the official Kakobuy account. Keep that distinction in mind when comparing recommendations or asking for help with an order.

sections.heading: Check what the product link actually identifies
paragraphs: Open the original seller listing before adding an item to your shortlist. Compare the photos, title, selectable colours, sizes and included pieces. Some listings combine several products under a single link, and the lowest displayed price may belong to a different variant. A spreadsheet row cannot preserve every change a seller makes later. Treat the live listing and the final order form as the places to confirm the purchase.

Also distinguish a catalogue page number from a seller item number. A useful research link should lead you back to the intended source, rather than merely to a similar photograph. If the Kakobuy form cannot parse the URL, use the official manual purchase process or ask support to confirm the item. Do not silently replace a failed link with another seller’s listing and assume that the product, sizing and return conditions remain the same.

sections.heading: Separate listing photos from order-specific inspection
paragraphs: A clear photograph is useful for discovering shape, colour and visible design details, but its origin matters. Seller photos, catalogue images and warehouse inspection photos serve different purposes. Unless a picture is explicitly tied to an inspected order, it should not be treated as evidence of the condition of your future item. On this site, catalogue photos are source-listing images; they are not automatically labelled as warehouse QC.

After an item reaches the warehouse, compare its order-specific photos with the colour, size and quantity you selected. If an important detail is missing, ask whether a targeted photograph or measurement is available and what it costs. A photo can help you spot an obvious mismatch; it cannot by itself establish authenticity, fabric composition, durability or comfort. A good spreadsheet explains these limits instead of treating every attractive picture as proof of quality.

sections.heading: Prefer useful categories and measurements over endless lists
paragraphs: Categories should help you compare like with like. A jacket, a lightweight shirt and a matching set need different checks, even when all appear under clothing. Use category pages to narrow the search, then open only the candidates that match your intended use. For clothing, a seller’s measurement method is usually more useful than a familiar size letter. For shoes, the exact model’s chart matters more than a general conversion table.

Keep a small comparison note with the source URL, variant, relevant measurements, listed item price and unresolved question. This reduces repeated browsing and makes it easier to explain an issue to support later. If an entry has no size chart, uncertain materials or unclear contents, mark that gap instead of filling it with an assumption. The strongest shortlist is the one whose important uncertainties can be resolved before payment.

sections.heading: Look for meaningful updates, not just a fresh date
paragraphs: A recently dated page may still contain broken links, unavailable variants or outdated prices. Check whether updates correspond to something useful: a working seller link, a corrected description or a policy reference that still matches the official help page. No independent catalogue can promise that every seller listing will remain unchanged between your visit and your order. Recheck the details at the moment you commit to buying.

When a guide mentions fees, storage or returns, look for the official source and the conditions attached to the statement. A warehouse storage limit is not the same as a seller’s return window. An estimated delivery time is not a guaranteed arrival date. Prefer explanations that tell you which order status or shipping quote to inspect, rather than broad promises that cannot account for your item, destination or payment method.

sections.heading: Compare the full cost of a shortlist
paragraphs: The visible product price is only the beginning of a purchasing decision. Record the item and domestic delivery costs, then estimate international shipping with the intended destination, package weight and dimensions. Add packaging, optional services and any applicable route-specific taxes or charges. A cheaper item may create a larger or heavier parcel, while a compact alternative may suit your budget better after the complete shipping quote is available.

Use the official shipping estimator to compare plausible scenarios rather than inventing a precise total from a catalogue photo. Before warehouse arrival, the packed dimensions may be uncertain. After arrival, review the actual measurements and the chosen line’s restrictions. If you compare spreadsheets, compare their clarity about these costs as well as the products they feature. A low headline price does not establish the cheapest delivered option.

sections.heading: Understand recommendations and commercial links
paragraphs: A recommendation should explain its evidence and purpose. A category roundup can help you find relevant listings without claiming that every item was personally tested. An affiliate link may support a website, but it does not prove a product’s quality or make the site the seller. Read the disclosure and verify the official destination before entering account details or paying. Kakobuy Pick’s purchase links open the official item flow.

Be cautious with unsupported claims such as guaranteed fit, verified authenticity or the best seller for everyone. Useful editorial guidance tells you what to measure, what to inspect and what remains unknown. Your priorities may differ from another buyer’s: layering space, a particular closure, a removable insole or a smaller parcel can matter more than popularity. Keep those priorities visible while comparing the shortlist.

A simple comparison routine can keep research focused. Open the same category on each catalogue, choose a candidate, and follow it through to the seller page. Note whether you can identify the selected variant, find a usable measurement chart and distinguish the item price from delivery costs. Then read one relevant guide and check that its sources actually support the advice. You do not need to assign a score or declare a universal winner. The exercise reveals which resource gives you enough information for your next action and which leaves gaps you must resolve elsewhere. Repeat the check when an old bookmark stops working or when your requirements change. A spreadsheet that helped with a previous order may still need fresh verification for a new seller, product type or shipping destination.

sections.heading: Turn your research into a manageable order
paragraphs: Before ordering, revisit each shortlisted source and confirm stock, variant and quantity. Save the information that would be difficult to reconstruct if a seller edits the listing. Once the order arrives in the warehouse, review the available inspection photos promptly and resolve important discrepancies while any applicable return window is still open. Do not postpone a return decision merely because you plan to consolidate several products later.

Use the spreadsheet for discovery, the sizing and QC guides for checks, and the official account for transaction status. For a first shortlist, choose a few items whose specifications you can actually verify rather than collecting dozens of uncertain links. The practical value of a Kakobuy spreadsheet is the quality of the decisions it helps you make, from identifying a listing to understanding the final parcel quote.

sections.heading: Choose the job your jacket needs to do
paragraphs: Jacket research becomes easier when you start with how you intend to wear the garment. A lightweight layer for commuting, a loose outer layer over a hoodie and a structured jacket for occasional wear need different proportions and details. Write down your priorities before browsing: layering room, sleeve coverage, pockets, closure type and the conditions in which you expect to use it. The Kakobuy Pick jacket category is a place to discover source links and compare listing images. This guide is a selection method, not a claim that the listed jackets have been purchased, tested or authenticated by the editorial team. Open the original seller page for each candidate and check the exact variant. Product availability, specifications and prices can change independently of a catalogue entry.

sections.heading: Measure a comparable jacket you already own
paragraphs: Lay a well-fitting jacket flat using a consistent method. Record the chest width, shoulder width, sleeve length and back length, and note where each measurement begins and ends. Choose a reference garment with a similar construction and enough room for the layers you plan to wear. A fitted blazer is a poor measurement reference for a loose insulated jacket because the intended shape and internal space differ.

Compare these values with the seller’s chart for the exact listing. Check whether the chart describes garment measurements or body measurements, and whether chest is given as a flat width or a circumference. Do not double a number unless the method requires it. If the seller does not explain the chart, request clarification before selecting a variant. A familiar size label is not evidence that the proportions match your reference garment.

sections.heading: Read construction and material details carefully
paragraphs: Look beyond the outer photograph to the lining, cuffs, hem, hood and fastening system. A lining can affect how a jacket slides over another layer, while a tight cuff or hem can change the usable fit even when the chest seems generous. Check whether a hood is attached or removable, whether pockets have closures and whether accessories shown in the photo are included in the selected item.

Treat material descriptions as seller claims unless independent evidence is available. A close-up image may show a texture, but it cannot establish fibre composition, insulation performance or waterproof protection. Terms such as technical, premium or winter-ready are not a substitute for specific product information. If a performance claim is essential to your decision, ask what supports it rather than inferring it from the appearance of a fabric or a brand-style design.

sections.heading: Compare colours, variants and included pieces
paragraphs: Seller listings sometimes place several jacket styles or fabric options on the same page. Confirm that the price and size chart apply to the colour and construction you intend to order. A thumbnail selected during browsing may not be the variant carried into the order form. Recheck the variant text, photograph and quantity before payment, especially when the listing includes a matching set or a detachable component.

Save the original seller URL and your chosen specifications in a short note. This gives you a reference if the listing changes or if a warehouse photograph appears inconsistent. A catalogue identifier is useful for navigating this site, but it may not be the original seller’s product identifier. Use the seller source and the official order number when explaining a mismatch to support.

sections.heading: Ask inspection questions that photos can answer
paragraphs: When the jacket reaches the warehouse, first compare the item with the order: colour, size label, visible construction and included pieces. Review front and back views, closures, seams and any area that matters to your purchase. If a zipper, cuff or printed detail is hidden, ask whether a closer photograph is available. A specific question is more useful than an open-ended request to confirm that everything is good.

If fit remains uncertain, ask for a measurement using clearly defined endpoints and check any service charge before requesting it. Ordinary inspection is not a tailoring assessment. The official inspection guidance limits what photos and surface checks can establish; colour differences, measurement variation and actual use performance remain important uncertainties. Do not treat a warehouse image as a guarantee of authenticity, warmth, waterproofing or comfort.

sections.heading: Include packed volume in your shipping estimate
paragraphs: Jackets can occupy substantial space even when their item price looks modest. The selected shipping line may consider both actual weight and volumetric weight, so package dimensions matter. Use the official estimator with realistic inputs and check the line’s current billing rules. Before warehouse measurement, treat your numbers as a planning scenario. After arrival, compare the measured item and proposed packaging with the quote.

Ask about packaging changes only when you understand their trade-offs. Removing unnecessary outer packaging may reduce space, but protective packaging can matter for structure, delicate finishes or accessories. Compression is not automatically suitable for every material or construction. Decide what protection you need, then compare the resulting parcel options. Do not assume that the cheapest listed jacket will also be the cheapest jacket to receive.

sections.heading: Make a useful shortlist instead of chasing a ranking
paragraphs: Compare candidates in the same order: intended use, measurements, construction, selected variant and total cost. For example, one candidate may have a clear chart but an uncertain lining description, while another has detailed material information but no shoulder measurement. Record the missing evidence and ask whether it can be obtained. This is an editorial comparison exercise, not a report of a tested purchase.

A useful jacket find is one that matches your requirements with manageable uncertainty. Popularity or an attractive photo does not remove the need to check proportions and seller conditions. If neither candidate provides the information you need, keep looking rather than choosing the one with the most confident description. You can return to the jacket category with a narrower search once you know which detail is holding up the decision.

When comparing two sizes, describe the practical difference instead of asking which label is normally correct. One option may provide more chest room but also a longer sleeve or a lower hem. Compare those changes with the way your reference jacket sits when you reach forward, sit down or wear your intended inner layer. These observations help you decide which measurements matter most; they do not turn a flat chart into a guarantee of movement or comfort. If the seller chart does not explain a critical dimension, pause the comparison until the method is clear. It is often more useful to resolve one missing shoulder or sleeve measurement than to collect many unrelated product photos. Keep the result in your shortlist so that the eventual warehouse review answers the same question you had before ordering.

sections.heading: Resolve warehouse issues before planning the final parcel

Keep tags and packaging suitable for resale while the issue is being decided. The longer warehouse storage period does not extend a shorter return request deadline.

Once you decide to keep the jacket, combine its measured size and weight with any other items you intend to ship. Confirm destination restrictions, packaging choices and the current route quote in the official account. Save the final product and parcel details for later reference. This sequence connects the initial jacket link to a checked variant and an informed shipping decision without pretending that a catalogue can guarantee the outcome.

articles.title: Kakobuy Sneaker Finds: Size Charts, QC Photos and Source Links
articles.description: Compare sneaker links using the exact model’s size chart, clear photo checks and packaging choices. Understand what warehouse QC can and cannot confirm.

sections.heading: Start with use and fit requirements
paragraphs: A sneaker shortlist should begin with what you need from the shoes: everyday wear, a particular silhouette, space for your usual socks or compatibility with an insole you already use. Write down the fit issues you want to avoid, such as pressure across the forefoot or insufficient toe room. A visually similar shoe may use a different last or construction, so appearance alone is a weak guide to how it will feel.

The shoe category on Kakobuy Pick provides product links and listing photos for research. This guide does not represent a set of shoes purchased or tested by the editorial team, and inclusion in the catalogue is not an authenticity certificate. Open the original seller listing, check the precise model and variant, and verify the information that matters to your own purchase before using the official Kakobuy order flow.

sections.heading: Keep foot length and shoe measurements separate
paragraphs: Measure your feet using a repeatable method and the socks you expect to wear, following any method specified by the seller. Record the longer foot and any fit considerations that a simple length cannot capture. Compare the result with the chart for the exact model. A generic regional size conversion may be useful background, but it does not replace the seller’s model-specific information or explain differences in width and shape.

Foot length, insole length and outsole length describe different things. An outsole photograph cannot establish the space inside the shoe, and an insole measurement may be affected by shape or measurement technique. If a chart uses an unclear term, ask what was measured. Avoid turning an uncertain number into a confident size recommendation. Your reference pair can be helpful only when you compare like measurements and acknowledge differences in construction.

sections.heading: Verify the exact seller link and selected option
paragraphs: Check the original listing for the model, colour, size range and included accessories. Some pages combine several versions under one link or show a starting price that applies to a particular option. Confirm that the variant selected in the Kakobuy form matches your intended purchase. Pay attention to quantity as well: an order should clearly describe the pair or other unit the seller supplies.

Save the source URL and the selected variant text before payment. A local catalogue number is not necessarily the seller’s item number, and a similar thumbnail is not enough to prove that two links refer to the same offer. If the link cannot be parsed, use the official manual purchase route or ask support to confirm the exact source. Do not assume that a replacement link has the same sizing, stock or return terms.

sections.heading: Use a structured warehouse photo review
paragraphs: Once the shoes arrive in the warehouse, start with the order identity: model, colour, size labels and included pieces. Then compare the visible condition of both shoes. Look at the toe area, sides, heels, sole edges, stitching and closures in the photographs that are available. Lighting and camera angle can affect how colours and shapes appear, so ask for a specific additional view when an important point is unclear.

Keep your questions tied to visible evidence. A photo can help identify a mismatched label, an obvious mark or a missing accessory, but it cannot establish long-term durability, internal construction or comfort during wear. The official inspection guidance describes limits to surface checks and measurement accuracy. Ordinary warehouse QC should not be presented as authentication or a guarantee that the shoes will perform as the seller describes.

sections.heading: Request measurements only when they resolve a decision
paragraphs: Before requesting an extra service, explain the uncertainty you are trying to resolve. If an insole is removable and a measurement service is available, ask how the measurement will be taken and what it costs. A photograph should show the relevant endpoints clearly enough to interpret. Do not compare a curved surface measurement with a straight-line value without understanding the difference.

An extra measurement is useful when it changes a decision about keeping the item; it is not a substitute for an adequate size chart before purchase. The width, upper shape and internal volume can still affect fit even when length appears suitable. Avoid collecting more photos simply to postpone an uncertain return decision. If the remaining issue cannot be answered through available inspection, consider the seller’s terms and your tolerance for that uncertainty.

sections.heading: Compare box protection with parcel size
paragraphs: A shoe box can protect the shape and help retain accessories, but it also adds material and volume to a parcel. Decide whether keeping it matters for your purchase before requesting packaging changes. Removing a box may reduce space, yet the shoes still need appropriate protection against crushing or rubbing. Ask about the available packaging options and their charges rather than assuming that every service or change is included.

Use the actual warehouse measurements and the chosen shipping line’s billing rules when comparing options. A line may charge according to volumetric weight as well as actual weight. Box removal therefore does not create a predictable saving in every case. Compare the complete quote, including protection you still need, and check destination and route restrictions in the official account before submitting the parcel.

sections.heading: Build a comparison note that keeps evidence visible
paragraphs: For each candidate, record the source URL, selected size, chart method, listed price and unresolved fit question. Add whether the listing explains the materials and what is included. When warehouse inspection becomes available, record what was confirmed and what remains uncertain. Separating seller information from order-specific observations prevents a promotional description from becoming an assumed fact in your own notes.

For example, a candidate with a clear chart and a matching label may be easier to assess than one with only lifestyle photos, but that still does not prove comfort or authenticity. This is a method for comparing evidence, not a tested ranking. If your requirements depend on a claim that cannot be verified through the listing or available inspection, do not let popularity or an apparently low price replace that missing information.

It also helps to separate visual preferences from requirements that affect daily use. A colour or profile may be clear in a listing, while heel hold, forefoot room and how the upper bends remain uncertain until wear. Record those limits rather than describing the candidate as a confirmed fit. If you use a reference shoe, note the model and the measurement method instead of relying only on the regional size printed on its label. Different charts can assign similar labels to different dimensions, and similar dimensions can still produce different sensations because of shape and materials. This comparison gives you a more specific question for the seller or support team. It does not justify a universal instruction to size up or down for every buyer or every listing.

sections.heading: Act on discrepancies before the return window closes
paragraphs: Review the warehouse photos promptly, especially when the size label, colour or included pieces appear different from the order. Save the relevant image and explain the mismatch using the order number and original variant details. Ask support about eligibility, costs and the next step under the seller’s current conditions. Preserve tags, accessories and packaging while a return is being considered.

The period allowed for warehouse storage is separate from the shorter deadline for an eligible return request. Waiting for another item to arrive does not necessarily preserve your ability to send these shoes back. Once you decide to keep the pair, finalise the packaging and route quote using measured information. A good sneaker find is a source link that leads to an informed purchase decision, not a promise that every uncertainty has disappeared.

articles.title: How to use a Kakobuy spreadsheet without losing track of the details
articles.description: Build a useful shortlist, compare live seller links and keep price, variant and photo evidence attached to the right item.

sections.heading: Start with a decision, not a huge list
paragraphs: A Kakobuy spreadsheet is useful when it turns browsing into a specific purchasing decision. Start with one category, an item budget and the characteristics that matter to you. For a jacket, those may be length, fabric, lining and space for layers. For a bag, dimensions and closure may matter more than a familiar product name. A shortlist of three relevant listings is easier to verify than dozens of saved screenshots.

Kakobuy Pick reads the CnBuyCha catalogue for product details and prices. Its search and category filters help you narrow that catalogue; they do not rank a seller’s reliability. A popular result reflects browsing activity, not a verified count of completed purchases or a quality certification.

sections.heading: Keep a small record for each candidate
paragraphs: Record the original seller URL, the intended colour or style, the size, the quantity and the date you checked it. Save your own notes alongside the link. A title can appear on several listings, and the cheapest option displayed on a page may be a different variant. Your notes should let you return to the exact option without reconstructing the decision from memory.

A useful comparison has a separate column for unanswered questions. Write “measurement missing” or “domestic postage not checked” rather than quietly treating missing information as zero cost or a good fit. This makes the next action obvious and stops an attractive photograph from filling gaps in the evidence.

sections.heading: Use photos for the questions they can answer
paragraphs: Open the available gallery and look for the views needed for your decision. A front image may show colour and shape but not a zip, label or interior pocket. Zooming a low-resolution image cannot reveal details that were never captured. If a feature matters and the image does not show it, leave it unresolved.

Pictures on this site are CnBuyCha reference images. Their warehouse-QC provenance has not been verified. They should not be presented as photographs of the item you will receive. The official Kakobuy inspection rules also limit what warehouse checks establish; photos do not prove authenticity, functional performance or long-term durability.

sections.heading: Compare the full commitment
paragraphs: The displayed USD estimate is a starting point for comparison. Check the live variant price and seller-to-warehouse postage in Kakobuy, then keep international freight and optional services separate in your budget. A lower item price does not necessarily make the delivered order cheaper. A bulky item may create a larger parcel than a slightly more expensive compact alternative.

Do not invent a shipping figure just to complete your comparison. Mark it as an estimate until you have usable weight and dimensions. Recheck the total once the actual order reaches the warehouse and you can compare eligible routes.

sections.heading: Reopen the source before committing
paragraphs: Use Open in Kakobuy and compare the loaded page with your shortlist. Check that the seller item, variant and quantity match. The official buying guide explains that some links may need manual entry; a failed import is a reason to verify the source, not to choose the nearest-looking result.

Make a final decision only after the unanswered questions are resolved or consciously accepted. Keep the order details so you can compare them with the warehouse arrival later. This simple record connects research, payment and inspection into one traceable process without treating the spreadsheet as a guarantee.

articles.description: Learn how Kakobuy product links relate to seller listings, check colour and size, and handle links that cannot be parsed with a manual purchase request.

sections.heading: Use the original listing as the final identity check
paragraphs: A spreadsheet link is a research shortcut. Before payment, compare the original seller listing with the Kakobuy order form: seller item, colour, size, quantity and included pieces should describe the same purchase. A local catalogue number is not necessarily the seller’s product number. Save the original listing and selected variant so that later photos can be checked against what you ordered.

The official buying guide supports pasting product links and provides a manual purchase route when a link cannot be parsed. Availability depends on the source and the particular URL, so an import error does not by itself prove that the item cannot be purchased. Avoid repeatedly substituting similar-looking items. Ask support to confirm the exact source, stock and specification, especially for mixed listings or minimum order quantities.

sections.heading: Follow the identity of the item
paragraphs: A purchase link is useful only if it carries the correct seller listing. Distinguish the original marketplace URL from the Kakobuy page that imports it and from the local catalogue URL you used to discover it. These are three different addresses with different purposes. The local product number is not automatically the seller’s item number.

On Kakobuy Pick, Open in Kakobuy passes the known original seller URL to Kakobuy. After it opens, compare the actual title, pictures and options with the source. The existence of an affiliate parameter says nothing about stock, price or whether the import has selected the right variant.

sections.heading: Check the source before troubleshooting the agent page
paragraphs: If an imported product looks wrong, first reopen the original listing. Check whether the seller has changed the product, removed an option or stopped selling it. A saved link can remain reachable while its content changes. Keep a note of the seller item ID and the option you intended to buy.

When copying a link, use a specific product page rather than a shop home page, collection page or unrelated advertisement. If the seller uses a short sharing link, confirm what product it opens before submitting it. Avoid guessing missing item IDs from filenames, photographs or similar listings.

sections.heading: Automatic import is not a universal promise
paragraphs: Kakobuy’s official buying guide describes automatic capture for supported listings and a manual purchase form when necessary. It also gives platform-specific notes that do not justify claiming every Weidian, Taobao or 1688 URL always imports. The current product page and order flow are the practical checks for your particular listing.

An import failure may leave the price, options or delivery details incomplete. Do not fill those gaps with invented values. A search result from a different seller may be a different product even if the photograph looks identical. Verify the replacement separately before treating it as an alternative.

sections.heading: Prepare a manual order that can be understood
paragraphs: Use the actual seller URL and the item’s real name, selected size, colour, quantity and current price information. Include a concise note when an option name is ambiguous. The goal is to make the intended purchase unambiguous to the purchaser, not to paste every line of a sales page into the notes.

For example, “Black, size M, one piece; confirm the chest measurement in the seller chart before purchasing” is more useful than “the one in the photo.” This is an editorial example, not a required Kakobuy template. If you cannot establish the price or domestic postage, ask for clarification through the official flow.

sections.heading: Read quantity and price conditions carefully
paragraphs: The official guide specifically warns about minimum purchase quantities on 1688. A displayed price can depend on quantity or variant. Check whether your intended order meets the seller’s requirement before comparing it with a one-piece offer elsewhere. Also check whether the chosen quantity changes domestic postage.

Before paying, review the order summary as a whole: correct item, correct option, correct quantity and a complete purchase cost. Save the resulting order number and notes. If an issue appears later, these details help support compare the purchase request with the received item.

sections.heading: Read the conditions on the manual purchase form
paragraphs: Before applying this guidance, check the conditions shown for your exact order. The official manual purchase form currently warns that certain third-party links have no after-sales service and do not support refunds, cancellation or changes after payment. The general warehouse return process is therefore not available for every purchase. Clarify an uncertain variant, price or return condition before paying; do not assume that an inspection photo creates a return right.

Never substitute a local catalogue ID for a seller item ID.
Use manual entry only with real listing information.
Check minimum quantities and the final selected variant.

articles.title: Kakobuy QC photos: a practical inspection checklist and its limits
articles.description: Review visible order details, ask precise follow-up questions and separate reference images from the inspection of your own purchase.

sections.heading: Identify what you are actually looking at
paragraphs: Before judging a photo, establish its source. Seller photography, another buyer’s historical images and the pictures attached to your own warehouse order serve different purposes. A good-looking reference image does not prove that your item has arrived in the same condition. Keep the order number and selected variant visible while reviewing your own inspection.

The pictures on Kakobuy Pick come from CnBuyCha. We have not verified them as warehouse QC. Use them to research visible features, then use the photos associated with your own Kakobuy order to decide what needs checking before shipment.

sections.heading: Read the standard inspection scope
paragraphs: Kakobuy’s published inspection rules focus on visible details such as style, quantity, colour, size and model. They describe restrictions on opening sealed goods and on inspecting the contents of certain sealed non-clothing items. Treat this as a defined service scope, not a promise that every hidden problem has been tested.

The same rules exclude authenticity, functionality and quality assessments for specialised goods such as electronics from standard inspection. A photograph of a powered device would not, by itself, establish battery health, electrical safety or long-term reliability. Ask what a requested extra check can actually establish before relying on it.

sections.heading: Review identity before minor cosmetic details
paragraphs: Start with whether the received item matches the order at all. Compare the visible colour, style, label, model and number of pieces with the selected option. For a set, confirm that all expected components are represented. For a pair, look at both items. This prevents a small stitching discussion from distracting you from an incorrect variant.

Next inspect the views for visible damage, stains, uneven construction or missing parts. A photograph may hide a surface, distort proportions or shift colour under lighting. Describe the uncertainty precisely instead of turning an unclear image into a definite defect claim.

sections.heading: Request evidence that answers one question
paragraphs: A focused request is easier to act on: ask for the label, the relevant closure, the inside pocket or a clearly positioned measurement. State which order and which part you mean. Confirm availability and any charge for extra photographs or measurements through Kakobuy before assuming the service is included.

For a measurement photo, explain the start and end points and whether you need a flat width or circumference. A ruler placed at an angle or a garment stretched differently can give a misleading comparison. Your request should make the method reproducible, especially if you are comparing it with an item you already own.

sections.heading: Decide before changing the packaging
paragraphs: If something does not match, save the relevant images and contact the purchaser through the order message area. Keep the original tags and packaging while the issue is assessed. The return rules include condition requirements and exclusions for items whose packaging or labels have been removed.

Avoid approving a parcel simply because you have waited a long time. Equally, avoid assuming every visible irregularity qualifies for a free return. Separate an established mismatch from a preference or an unresolved question, then ask for the available remedy and its cost before deciding.

Ask one precise question when a view is missing.

articles.title: Kakobuy Size Guide: Measure Clothes & Shoes Before Buying
articles.description: Compare Kakobuy size charts with clothes that fit. Learn flat chest, sleeve and foot measurements, then request the specific warehouse check you need.

sections.heading: How to choose a Kakobuy size before paying
paragraphs: Open the size chart for the exact seller listing and selected variant. Measure a similar item that already fits, using the same start and end points as that chart. For tops, compare chest width, body length and sleeve reach; for trousers, compare waist, rise and inseam. Record the units and whether the chart describes flat clothing, circumference or the body. If the measurement method is missing, ask before ordering.

For footwear, measure both feet and use the longer foot when reading the seller’s guidance. Keep foot length separate from insole and outsole length. Kakobuy’s official size guidance says seller standards vary, so a familiar size label or a general conversion cannot guarantee fit. Ask for the exact missing measurement while a return is still possible; a standard inspection photo of the size label does not establish comfort.

sections.heading: There is no universal Kakobuy size chart
paragraphs: Kakobuy is the purchasing intermediary; the seller and the particular product determine the available sizes. A letter such as M or L is not enough to compare two unrelated listings. Even a familiar model name may be offered by different sellers with different measurements or options. Start with the chart for the exact listing you intend to order.

This guide offers a practical comparison method rather than a guaranteed conversion between countries or brands. Do not automatically size up or down because a comment about another product recommends it. Use measurements and intended fit to make the decision.

sections.heading: Create a reference you can repeat
paragraphs: Choose a garment you already wear comfortably and measure it flat without stretching. For a top, useful points include chest width, shoulder width, sleeve length and body length. For trousers, record waist measurement, rise and leg length using the same approach as the seller’s chart. Note the units and the measurement positions.

Flat width and circumference are not interchangeable. A 54 cm flat chest width is a different kind of measurement from a 54 cm chest circumference. Do not double or halve a number until the chart’s method is clear. If the seller’s diagram is unclear, ask before placing the order.

sections.heading: Compare fit, fabric and the intended use
paragraphs: Two garments with similar measurements can feel different because of cut, stretch, thickness and layering. A jacket worn over a hoodie needs a different decision from a close-fitting base layer. Compare the shape of the garment as well as the numbers; a wide body with short sleeves is not equivalent to a longer, narrower cut.

Write down the difference between the reference and the listing. For example, a listing that is 2 cm wider and 3 cm shorter than your reference presents a specific fit trade-off. Those numbers are an illustrative comparison, not a recommendation that this amount of difference will suit everyone.

sections.heading: Treat footwear and accessories separately
paragraphs: For footwear, check which sizing system the listing uses and what its length measurement describes. Foot length, insole length and outsole length are different measurements. A conversion chart cannot resolve width, toe shape or personal comfort. Use the exact seller’s information and ask for clarification if the available numbers are ambiguous.

For a bag, consider width, height, depth, opening and strap length. A bag can have enough overall volume but an opening too small for the item you want to carry. For accessories, identify the dimension that affects use rather than assuming that a product photo communicates scale accurately.

sections.heading: Connect the sizing decision to inspection
paragraphs: Include the selected size and any important clarification in your order notes. When the item arrives, compare its visible label with the order. The official inspection rules include size information among the visible checks, but that does not mean standard inspection proves a comfortable fit or includes every measurement you might want.

If you need a measurement photograph, ask about the method, availability and cost before relying on it. Raise a mismatch while the return question can still be considered and keep tags and packaging. A careful sizing record is useful evidence; it does not remove seller conditions or guarantee a free exchange.

sections.heading: Turn a size chart into a decision
paragraphs: For a hoodie or football shirt, write the reference garment’s chest width and length beside the seller’s values. Mark any difference you actually want, such as more room for layering or a shorter body. Check sleeve construction before comparing sleeve numbers. A dropped shoulder and a conventional shoulder seam can use different starting points, so identical numbers do not necessarily produce identical reach.

If the seller provides only a height-and-weight suggestion, ask for garment measurements when fit is important. For shoes, ask which length the chart represents and whether a model-specific width description is available. Record the unresolved measurement before ordering; then request that exact check at the warehouse if necessary. The goal is a clear comparison, not a universal conversion from one brand’s size letter to another.

sections.heading: Use a measurement difference to make a specific decision
paragraphs: Consider a reference garment with comfortable chest room but sleeves that feel too short. Compare chest and sleeve differences separately against the seller chart; do not reduce the decision to a single instruction to size up. Confirm that both sleeve measurements use the same starting point. If the chart uses a different method, ask for the missing measurement before treating the numbers as comparable.

Keep the selected variant beside the measurement note and compare it again when order-specific images arrive. A matching size label does not confirm the garment’s measured dimensions. If a measurement is essential, ask whether the warehouse can provide that exact check and whether it has a charge. Make the request early enough to act under the purchase conditions that apply.

Record units and whether a measurement is flat or around the body.
Compare with a well-fitting reference using the same method.
Keep the selected option and any clarification in your order notes.

articles.title: Kakobuy Weight & Shipping Calculator: Estimate Parcel Cost
articles.description: Calculate actual and volumetric parcel weight, compare route divisors and check a live Kakobuy shipping quote. Includes a weight calculator and packing examples.

sections.heading: How to use a Kakobuy weight and shipping calculator
paragraphs: Enter the packed parcel weight and its length, width and height in the calculator below. Select the divisor stated by the intended shipping line. Where a route bills the greater of actual and volumetric weight, the larger result is the starting point for its weight charge. A weight result is not a shipping price: the current route quote determines rates, minimums, rounding and available services.

Next, open the official Kakobuy estimator with your destination, goods type and measured parcel inputs. Compare eligible lines using the same packing assumptions, then check handling charges and any optional services. If you only know item weights, label the result provisional and recalculate after packing. Do not compare an unpacked estimate with a measured box and treat the difference as a confirmed saving.

sections.heading: Keep grams and kilograms consistent
paragraphs: The estimator asks for weight in grams. A parcel weighing 4 kg should therefore be represented as 4000 g in that field. Write down your assumptions when you do not yet know the final packed weight. Product-only weight excludes some packing materials, while a rough shopping-list estimate may miss boxes and accessories entirely.

When warehouse information becomes available, replace estimates with the better figures. Do not compare a packed weight on one route with an unboxed product estimate on another and call the difference a discount. Both quotations should describe the same intended parcel.

sections.heading: Calculate volumetric weight using the route’s divisor
paragraphs: Kakobuy’s official explanation describes volumetric weight as length × width × height in centimetres divided by the carrier-specific divisor. Its examples mention several possible divisors. It then compares volumetric and actual weight for applicable routes. The important step is reading the divisor and billing conditions of the particular line.

As an editorial example, a 40 × 30 × 30 cm box has a volume of 36,000 cubic centimetres. Dividing by 6000 gives 6 kg; dividing by 5000 gives 7.2 kg. If actual weight is 4 kg and the route charges the greater figure, those assumptions produce 6 kg or 7.2 kg of chargeable weight. These are weight calculations, not shipping prices.

sections.heading: Compare like for like
paragraphs: Use the same destination, contents, weight and dimensions when comparing routes. Then record the quoted total, relevant restrictions, estimated transit window and any optional service you actually want. Read whether a displayed amount is an initial estimate and how the final parcel is measured or adjusted.

A headline price alone cannot tell you whether the service fits your needs. A higher quote may accompany different delivery handling or conditions; a lower quote may involve restrictions that matter to your parcel. Choose based on the complete terms presented in the current quotation rather than an unsupported “best line” claim.

sections.heading: Recheck after packing decisions
paragraphs: Removing a box, adding reinforcement or combining items can change dimensions and weight. Request a revised comparison when a change is material. A reduction in volumetric weight may help, but it is not a reason to remove protection required by a fragile item. Keep the physical contents and protection needs in the decision.

Save the inputs and quotation date so you know what the estimate described. The official estimator notes that third-party carriers can adjust rates. An old quote or someone else’s parcel screenshot is therefore a reference, not a price commitment for your shipment.

sections.heading: What should you enter when the weight is still unknown?
paragraphs: Before warehouse measurement, create a light and a heavy planning scenario and note which values are estimates. Include the packaging and all intended contents. Use both scenarios in the official estimator with the same destination and goods type. If the cost changes enough to affect your purchase decision, wait for better information rather than presenting a rough product weight as a precise shipping quote.

The weight comparison on this page illustrates the calculation only. It does not know the current route rate, billing increments, minimum charge, surcharge or contents restrictions. Read those conditions in the official quote and update the inputs after packing. An accurate multiplication can still give an unsuitable budget if the chosen divisor or package measurements do not match the actual service.

sections.heading: Compare quotations using the same parcel assumptions
paragraphs: When comparing routes, hold the destination, goods type, packed weight and dimensions constant. Record whether each quotation includes the services you intend to choose, and note any rounding or minimum charge stated by the route. A comparison using unpacked weight on one route and packed weight on another can produce an apparent saving that disappears at submission.

The calculator on this page compares weights only. It cannot establish route availability, an exchange rate or a payable shipping amount. If you change the packaging, update the official estimate before making a decision. Keep the earlier estimate and the accepted parcel quote as separate records so that later adjustments can be traced to the changed inputs.

checklist: Use the actual destination, goods type and dimensions.
Enter grams where the estimator requests grams.
Read the divisor and billing rules for the selected route.
Refresh the quote after meaningful packing changes.

articles.title: Kakobuy Fees: Item Cost, Shipping, Packaging and Payment
articles.description: Build a Kakobuy cost checklist covering the item, domestic shipping, international shipping, packaging and payment. Check route-specific taxes before paying.

sections.heading: Separate basic service fees from route-specific charges
paragraphs: The official services page describes basic purchasing without a handling fee. This does not remove the cost of the item, domestic transport, international delivery, packaging or optional services. Another cost page lists ¥8 for packaging materials. Because the official pages use different labels for that amount, do not automatically add the same ¥8 twice. Match each line to the current order or parcel checkout and ask support about any unclear charge.

A June 2026 announcement described a €3 per-parcel EU tariff arrangement included in shipping; it was not a general shopping-agent service fee. A later June 2026 notice said EU Duty-Free Shipping Lines include applicable duties and taxes, with additional tariffs borne by Kakobuy. These notices concern particular routes and circumstances. Use the current quote and conditions of the route you actually select; do not apply an EU announcement to every country or shipping line.

sections.heading: Separate the purchase from the parcel
paragraphs: The first useful budget distinction is between buying the item and sending it internationally. Kakobuy’s official buying guide treats these as separate stages. The purchase includes the seller’s item price and domestic postage to the warehouse. A later parcel submission introduces the international route and the services selected for that shipment.

A price on Kakobuy Pick is the USD estimate displayed by CnBuyCha, not a payable all-inclusive invoice. The selected variant, quantity and live seller price may differ from the catalogue reference. Keep that distinction clear when comparing items or planning a larger order.

sections.heading: Read fee labels in context
paragraphs: The official services page advertises zero service fees while still identifying product, international shipping and declaration-related costs. Another cost-calculation page uses packing and optional-service terminology. These pages should not be collapsed into a claim that every possible charge is zero or that one fixed amount applies to every route.

Use the current checkout and parcel quotation as the decision record. If a label is unclear, ask what it covers and whether it is already included in another amount. This is particularly useful when comparing a purchase-stage subtotal with a later shipping-stage total: the two numbers describe different commitments.

sections.heading: Use a budget with known and unknown amounts
paragraphs: List the item cost, domestic postage, expected international freight and any optional services separately. Add payment or conversion charges only when you can identify them in the actual payment flow. Leave unknown amounts clearly marked as estimates instead of hiding them inside a single apparently precise total.

For illustration, an item amount of 30 USD, domestic postage of 3 USD and an international quote of 18 USD produce a 51 USD subtotal before other applicable charges. These are invented arithmetic inputs for explanation, not Kakobuy prices. If the shipping input is only a guess, the subtotal remains a planning estimate.

sections.heading: Check the payment amount and currency
paragraphs: The official top-up guidance describes multiple methods, currency conversion and method-specific charges. Availability and conditions should be checked in your account at the time of payment. A familiar payment logo does not guarantee that the same method, currency or charge is available for every country or account.

Compare the amount being paid, the balance being credited and the currency conversion shown. Your payment provider may present its own conversion decision. Keep a receipt of the confirmed transaction and avoid comparing a converted account balance with a different currency amount as though they were identical.

sections.heading: Keep a record for later adjustments
paragraphs: Save the purchase summary and parcel quote separately. If a shipping adjustment or refund appears, this makes it easier to identify which stage it relates to. A refund credited to an account balance is not the same event as money arriving back at an external payment method; check the applicable process before assuming completion.

A sensible budget also leaves room for an unresolved cost before buying more items. The goal is not to predict every charge perfectly at the browsing stage. It is to know which amounts are confirmed, which are provisional and which decision will reveal the missing information.

checklist: Separate item purchase and international parcel expenses.
Review the current breakdown rather than a single fee headline.
Keep payment currency and credited balance distinct.
Save receipts and identify where any refund is credited.

articles.title: Kakobuy Warehouse: Storage Limits & Order Status
articles.description: Check the 100-day storage rule, 90-day reminder and separate 60-day unmatched-parcel period. Find the next step when a delivered order is not stored.

sections.heading: Check the order status before counting storage days
paragraphs: For normal goods, Kakobuy describes 100 days of storage from the in storage status, with a reminder at 90 days. Unmatched or incomplete forwarding parcels have a separate 60-day period from Signed for. Record the status date of each item, because goods that arrive together in your shopping plan may reach the warehouse on different days. A domestic delivered scan alone does not confirm the item is inspected and available for international shipment.

If delivery is recorded but the item is missing from stored goods, send support the order number, domestic tracking reference and delivery event. Ask whether ownership matching, receipt or inspection is pending. Keep that issue separate from a return decision: eligible warehouse returns normally require a request within the separate 5-day window. Do not let a storage allowance delay an urgent inspection or seller return request.

sections.heading: Track each item, not just the newest arrival
paragraphs: A warehouse can make a multi-seller order easier to organise, but the items do not necessarily arrive on the same day. Build a small record containing each order number, arrival or stored date, status and the next action. Waiting for the final item should not make you lose sight of the oldest one.

Use the dates and status displayed in your own Kakobuy account. A seller’s dispatch date is not necessarily the date that starts the warehouse storage clock. When the status is unclear, ask support which date applies rather than estimating from a domestic tracking screenshot.

sections.heading: Read the normal storage rule with its conditions
paragraphs: The official storage page checked on 17 October 2026 states a 100-day period for normal purchasing and forwarding parcels, starting from stored status. It describes a reminder after 90 days and warns about disposal after expiry when there has been no parcel submission or feedback. Confirm the current rule and the individual deadline before planning to wait.

A reminder is a useful extra signal, not a substitute for your own record. Keep contact information current and do not assume that an unread email, a holiday or an intention to purchase more goods automatically extends storage. Ask about your options before a deadline becomes urgent.

sections.heading: Resolve unmatched arrivals promptly
paragraphs: The same official page treats abnormal parcels differently. It describes a 60-day period from receipt for arrivals without the necessary order or complete logistics information, and explains that unmatched ownership can prevent reminders. This is a separate case from a normal order already associated with your account.

If a forwarding parcel has arrived but you cannot match it to an order, prepare the real tracking number, sender details and purchase evidence. Use the official account or support process to resolve the association. Do not create guessed records or assume an unknown parcel will be safely held indefinitely.

sections.heading: Storage time is not return time
paragraphs: Warehouse storage and seller return eligibility answer different questions. Storage concerns how long the goods remain held; returns concern whether a seller will take an item back under the applicable conditions. Kakobuy’s published five-day return rules contain eligibility, timing and condition requirements that are much shorter than normal storage.

Review an item soon after arrival, particularly if its size, colour or condition is uncertain. Keeping it in storage does not pause every seller deadline. Avoid postponing inspection until all the other items arrive if that means an earlier item’s return window may close.

sections.heading: Plan the next action before combining items
paragraphs: Once the items have been checked, compare shipping them together with splitting them into suitable parcels. Use actual contents, dimensions and route restrictions in that comparison. Do not hold a resolved item solely to chase a hypothetical saving that has never been quoted.

Keep a clear next action for every line in your record: await seller dispatch, inspect, ask a question, request a return, or submit a parcel. This makes a larger order manageable and helps you decide when waiting no longer serves the purchase plan. It is an editorial organisation method, not a promise of additional storage services.

sections.heading: How long does an order take to reach the warehouse?
paragraphs: Time to the warehouse is different from time allowed in storage. Seller preparation and domestic delivery happen before warehouse receipt; inspection and account updates follow their own workflow. Check seller dispatch and domestic tracking first. A delivered scan needs to be matched to your order before you assume the item is available to submit in an international parcel.

If the carrier shows delivery but the order has not appeared as stored, provide the domestic tracking number, delivery event and order number to support. Ask whether receipt, ownership matching or inspection is pending. Do not start a storage countdown from a guessed seller dispatch date or treat the normal 100-day allowance as a promise about processing speed.

sections.heading: Choose the next action from the nearest deadline
paragraphs: Review each stored item against both its storage deadline and any applicable return deadline. Mark it ready to ship only after the selected variant and visible condition have been checked. If an item has an unresolved issue, contact support now instead of waiting for the rest of a planned parcel. Keep a separate note for goods you intend to retain and goods awaiting a seller decision.

For a practical comparison, imagine that a jacket is ready but another seller has not dispatched a pair of shoes. Waiting might change the parcel cost, but that possible saving does not resolve the jacket’s return deadline. Check the immediate decision first, then compare the parcel options using realistic packed measurements. Do not describe an assumed combined-parcel saving as a confirmed amount.

checklist: Record the status and deadline of every order separately.
Check the current normal and abnormal-parcel rules.
Resolve missing forwarding information promptly.
Review return eligibility long before storage expires.
